identity.title: Fleet of Agents: Coordinated Problem Solving with Large Language Models

summary: Two demonstrated released-implementation defects affect cost accounting and WebShop selection; historical experimental impact remains unverified.

problems.title: Merged physical API requests discard subsequent prompt-token usage
problems.claim: Appendix C.3 batching reduces repeated input cost; dollar cost is central to Sections5–6 comparisons.
assumptions: n27 identical-prompt completions split16+11 by released adapter
Two successful physical requests with1000 billable prompt tokens each
Frozen catalog rates1.2 dollars/million input and output; no additional discounts
problems.check: Independent rational usage calculation under physical-request and released merge rules.
problems.counterevidence: Single physical request is legitimately charged one prompt; provider discounts and historical implementation may differ; no invoices or historical request logs examined.
problems.core_dependency: Cost measurement is a principal axis of core efficiency contribution. Severity applies to the reachable released measurement path, not a proven reversal of published rankings.

correction.statement: Sum per-physical-request usage under explicit pricing; separate logical hypothetical shared-input estimate.
correction.repair_verification: Algebraically exact for specified usage model and restores finite fixture.

focused_check.method: Relevant frozen source passages/static source, existing actual check output and independent analytic integration; no author-code execution.
focused_check.conclusion: Distinct physical requests each incur prompt usage; the released merge retains only the first request's prompt tokens. The inspected driver reaches the split path. Summing physical-response usage repairs the accounting identity. Major is retained for the released central cost path; historical billed cost and score changes remain unknown.

problems.title: WebShop evaluation uses action newline stop and whole-response digit matching
problems.claim: Table6 evaluation stop=null and Prompt7 final one-to-ten score guide agent selection.
problems.location: PDF p19,pp23–25; run/webshop.py:32–62,131–132; src/agents/ws.py:197–219; resample and retained-record update
assumptions: Two complete valid final-score replies with intended values.1,.9
A explanation mentions100dollars; B explanation has no digit
No cached value; equal-age linear selection; no other retained states
problems.check: Independent exact string parser and newline truncation fixtures; analytic normalization including epsilon.
problems.result: Full replies produce1.0,.9 instead of.1,.9; newline-stop produces1.0,0.0. Ideal low-state selection increases.1→10/19; zero-state exclusion can leave only low-state candidate.
problems.counterevidence: Some model outputs avoid failure; actual output frequencies unknown; environment reward is not this parsed value; historical code may differ; LATS attribution retained.
problems.core_dependency: Evaluation and resampling are the central coordination mechanism. The released path can invert evaluator preference, regardless of whether final benchmark scores also change.

correction.statement: Use evaluation config and validated anchored final-line/structured score; distinguish missing score from zero.
correction.repair_verification: Independent complete-reply parser restores.1,.9; cannot reconstruct truncated score; no author patch or benchmark rerun.

focused_check.method: Relevant frozen source passages/static source, existing actual check output and independent analytic integration; no author-code execution.
focused_check.conclusion: Step-generation stop configuration is reused for evaluation, and the descending whole-response digit parser can consume explanatory prices. Epsilon weighting and optional zero exclusion do not remove the demonstrated selection distortion. Major remains limited to the released selection mechanism; the frequency in historical runs is not established.
